chapters.title: Getting Started
text: Barely Functional Contraptions makes power from mushrooms, light and empty space, and grows resources on sheep.
## The machine casing
Every machine is built around a Functional Machine Block: craft it from Blue Steel, copper ingots and redstone, and use it in the machine recipes.
## Blue Steel

Every contraption's recipe takes Blue Steel where it would take an Iron Ingot: craft one from an Iron Ingot and any wool. Nine make a Block of Blue Steel, which recipes take where they'd take a Block of Iron (and it gives the nine back).
## The loop
- Mycelial Generators burn mushrooms and water to make Forge Energy (FE).
- Infuse sheep with a resource (an iron ingot, a diamond...) at an Infusion Altar to change their wool.
- Shear them for resource wool, and turn the wool back into resources in a Mechanical Separator powered by FE.
- Mushroom sheep give the generators their fuel, which closes the loop.
Sneak and right-click a sheep with an empty hand to see what it is infused with. JEI and Jade, if installed, show recipes and machine details.

chapters.title: Wrench and Links
text: The Barely Functional Wrench links blocks without touching.
- Right-click a generator, then another generator, to link them into one network (up to 64 blocks apart).
- Sneak and right-click a block to remove its links. Sneak and right-click the air to clear your selection.
The generator's screen shows how it is connected.
The wrench also sets each side of a Fluid or Item Pipe: see Pipe Sides.
## Dismantling
Hit any contraption with the wrench to pick it up at once. It goes straight into your inventory with whatever was inside it, such as fuel, wool or what it made. What doesn't fit drops on the ground.

chapters.title: Woollen Armour
text: ## Woollen Armour
Knit a full set from wool, in the same shapes as leather armour: a Beanie (5 wool), a Jumper (8), Leggings (7) and Boots (4).

Each piece takes the colour of the wool it's made from. One colour gives that colour; mixed wool blends the colours, as dyes do on leather. You can dye it afterwards like leather, or wash it in a water cauldron to make it white again.

It's a little better than leather: more armour on the jumper and leggings, it lasts longer and takes enchantments better. It mends with any wool on an anvil, and keeps you from freezing in powder snow.
## Muffled
While you wear Woollen Boots you're Muffled: you make no sound. No footsteps, landings, eating or hurt sounds, and sculk sensors, shriekers and Wardens can't hear you.
Take the boots off and it wears off 2 seconds later.

chapters.title: Data Packs
text: Sheep resources are data: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/sheep_resources/<name>.json. They reload with /reload.
An appearance block gives any resource wings, extra heads, glowing, a bigger size, its own sounds and more.

Furnace heat sources are data too: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/furnace_heat/<name>.json names a sheep, an entity or a look such as on_fire, and its power. Boost items are the blaze_furnace_boost data map.
Wool Burner fuels are data too: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/wool_burner_fuel/<name>.json, each with an ingredient, a burn_time and a power.
A separating recipe whose ingredient matches a Wool Bale (barelyfunctionalcontraptions:wool_bale with its sheep_resource component) gives that bale its own outputs instead of the scaled-up wool ones.
## Commands
- /bfc list: every loaded resource.
- /bfc generate: a resource for every material in the modpack.
- /bfc generate item <item>: a resource fed with any item.
Every number in the mod can be changed in its config files, from the mod list's Config button.

chapters.title: Glow Panels
text: The Glow Panel makes power from the light falling on its top.
- In full sunlight it makes 60 FE/t, less at dawn, dusk and in rain, and nothing at night.
- Under block light it makes up to 40 FE/t. A Glow Lamp on it or above it gives the full amount, day or night, even underground.
- A glowing Glow Ink sheep standing next to it lights it up too.
Its cells glow brighter the more it makes: dim at dawn, dusk or in rain, half lit under a Glow Lamp at night, fully lit in the midday sun, and dark when it makes nothing.
It pushes its energy into blocks beside and below it.
## Glow Lamp
A full-brightness lamp made from glow ink sacs, glass and glowstone dust.

chapters.title: Wool Burner
text: The Wool Burner burns spare wool for power, one item at a time.
- Plain wool (any colour): 30 FE/t for 10 seconds.
- String: 30 FE/t for 2.5 seconds.
- Coal Wool: 120 FE/t for 20 seconds.
Right-click it with fuel to load it, put fuel in the slot in its window, or feed it with a hopper or pipe. Hoppers and pipes can't take fuel back out.
It stores 20,000 FE and pushes it into every block around it. While its buffer is full it waits before lighting the next item, so nothing is wasted.
A comparator reads how full its fuel slot is.
## Data packs
Fuels are data: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/wool_burner_fuel/<name>.json, each with an ingredient, a burn_time in ticks and a power in FE/t.

chapters.title: Sheep Treadmill
text: A belt for a sheep to walk on, two blocks long. Place it facing the way you want the sheep to walk: the wheat hangs at the far end, the generator housing is at your end.

Put Wheat or Hay Bales in it (right-click, or a hopper or pipe). While it has food and no sheep, it calls the nearest grown sheep within 8 blocks over, and the sheep hops onto the belt. You can also lead one on. The sheep walks for the wheat and turns the belt.
## Power
- 20 FE/t while a sheep walks. Each level of Speed adds a fifth more; Slowness takes as much off.
- A sheared sheep runs lighter: a quarter more.
- It pushes its power into the blocks around the generator housing, up to 200 FE/t, and stores 20,000 FE.
## Upkeep
- One Wheat lasts 30 seconds of walking, a Hay Bale four and a half minutes. Without food the sheep wanders off.
- After 2 minutes the sheep is worn out. It steps off and rests for 30 seconds before it will walk again; put a fresh sheep on meanwhile. Sheep bred for Endurance walk for longer.
- While its buffer is full the sheep stands still and eats nothing.
Lambs are too small for the belt.

chapters.title: Blaze Furnace
text: The Blaze Sheep Furnace makes power from the heat of Blaze sheep standing in the 5x5 area around it (the config's radius), on its own level or on top of it.
- One Blaze sheep gives 80 FE/t. Each extra one adds a little less: 150, 210 and 260 FE/t for two, three and four. It counts up to four.
- Only a sheep showing its blazing fleece counts. A sheared sheep or a lamb gives nothing until its wool grows back.
- In rain or water a sheep gives half.
- Right-click with a Blaze Rod to load it, or put rods in the boost slot in its window: each rod doubles the output for 30 seconds. Hoppers and pipes can fill it too.
- Its Blaze sheep stay close: one that wanders up to 4 blocks out of the area walks back in while the furnace has room for more. The outline shows this as a faint dashed box.
Shear the sheep for Blaze Rods, or leave the fleece on for power: that's the trade-off.
It pushes its energy into every block around it, and a comparator reads one level per 20 FE/t.
Right-click it with an empty hand to open its window. The fire in the middle column rises with the heat; each line is one more heat source, and its pip lights while that source is in use.
## Showing the area
Click the spyglass button in the furnace's, the Automatic Shears' or the Infusion Altar's window, or sneak-right-click any of them with an empty hand, to show or hide its working area.

chapters.title: Mycelial Generator
text: Burns red or brown mushrooms and water to make FE: 200 FE/t from brown mushrooms, 250 FE/t from red ones.
## Running it
- Give it water with a bucket, a bucket in its slot, a pipe, or a Fluid Reservoir placed next to it.
- Put mushrooms in the top slot. Hoppers and pipes can insert from any side.
- It pushes energy into cables and machines next to it.
## Networks
Generators that touch form a network, and every running member boosts the whole network's output exponentially.
## Mycelium
Running generators slowly turn nearby dirt into mycelium and sometimes sprout huge mushrooms, which gives you more fuel.

chapters.title: Static Generator
text: A generator two blocks tall, like a Van de Graaff generator. Sheep rubbing against Copper Combs in its pen build up static, and its copper dome collects the charge and arcs it into power.
Its pen is 5x5, centred on it. Put up to 4 Copper Combs in the pen; a sheep standing right next to a comb gets rubbed. Sneak-right-click it to outline the pen, and right-click it for its window.
## Power
- A grown sheep with its fleece on gives 100 FE/t. Copper sheep give 150 and Redstone sheep 125.
- Up to six count, each in full: 600 FE/t from plain sheep, 900 from Copper sheep.
- Sheared sheep give nothing, so give the pen grass to regrow their wool.
- The dome arcs into its buffer every 3 seconds. It stores 500,000 FE and pushes up to 2,000 FE/t out of every face of its base but the top.
## Copper Combs
- A fresh comb passes on all of a sheep's charge. As sheep rub against it, it oxidises like copper: exposed 75%, weathered 50%, oxidised 25%, about every 20 minutes of work.
- Scrape a comb with an axe to take it back a stage. Or wax it with Honeycomb: it stops ageing for good, but the wax insulates it a little (85%).
- A broken comb keeps its stage and its wax.
## Shocks
- If nothing takes its power, its buffer fills and the charge builds up in the dome. Past half full it shocks players and mobs in its pen, knocking them back.
- Each piece of Woollen Armour takes a quarter off a shock, and a full set stops it. Its sheep are never shocked.
- A comparator reads how charged its dome is (0-15).
## Making it
- Static Generator: a Lightning Rod on top; Copper Block, Redstone, Copper Block in the middle; wool, a Functional Machine Block and wool at the bottom.
- Copper Comb: three Copper Ingots over a Brush.

chapters.title: Zero Point Module
text: Place two modules facing each other, on a floor and ceiling or on two walls, with open space between them.
- They link with a beam and make 1,000 FE/t for every block of gap, up to 64 blocks.
- Take the energy from either end.
- Stained glass in the gap colours the beam.
- The beam burns anything that walks into it, and mobs it kills drop loot as if you had killed them.

chapters.title: Thermal Reaction Chamber
text: Makes power from the difference between hot and cold. Blaze sheep stand in a pen against its hot side, Snow sheep in a pen against its cold side, and water runs through the middle.

Looking at its gauge panel, the hot side (red vents) is on the left and the cold side (blue vents) on the right. Each pen is 5x5 and starts one block out from that side. Sneak-right-click it with an empty hand to outline both. Water and power go in and out of any face, but the back has the ports.
## Power
- A Blaze sheep matched by a Snow sheep is a pair. The first pair makes 2,500 FE/t and each one after it a little less: about 4,700 for two, 8,000 for four and 10,100 for six, the most it counts.
- Only grown sheep with their fleece on count.
- A Blaze Rod in the hot slot and Blue Ice in the cold slot each burn for 30 seconds. While both burn, the output doubles. Hoppers and pipes can fill both slots.
- It stores 2,000,000 FE and pushes up to 40,000 FE/t into the blocks around it.
## Keeping it balanced
The needle in its window shows the balance. Every sheep without a partner on the other side, or a boost burning alone, tips it one step and costs a quarter of the output.
- Running hot for 30 seconds causes a meltdown. The Blaze sheep are singed bare and it explodes like TNT.
- Running cold for 30 seconds freezes it solid. It encases itself in Packed Ice and won't restart until you mine every block of it away.
- Running balanced counts the danger back down. The danger bar under the needle shows how close it is, and a comparator reads it (0 is steady, 15 is about to go), so you can wire up a safety cut-off.
- With its buffer full it makes no power and uses no water, boosts or fleece, but its herds still heat and chill it: uneven herds still melt it down or freeze it.

- It keeps its herds close without upsetting them: a side with fewer sheep calls a stray back from up to 4 blocks away, and it only calls a new pair when a Blaze sheep and a Snow sheep are both waiting nearby.
## Upkeep
- Water: 250 mB a tick while it reacts, what five Fluid Reservoirs make. If it runs dry it stops and blasts scalding steam out of its front for a few seconds.
- Fatigue: after an hour of reacting, a sheep's fleece is spent and it stops counting. Infuse it again, at the Infusion Altar or by hand, to renew it.
If neither pen has a partner for the other, it just waits: a pen of Blaze sheep on their own can't melt it down.

chapters.title: Echo Chamber
text: A 3x3x3 generator. Warden sheep standing in front of its dish listen for vibrations, and it turns what they hear into power.

Place it facing you: the block you place is the middle of its front, and the rest fills the space behind and above (it won't place if anything's in the way). The listening pen is 5x5 and starts one block out from its dish. Sneak-right-click it to outline the pen, and right-click it for its window. Breaking any part takes it all down, and you need a pickaxe to keep it.
## Power
- One grown Warden sheep with its fleece on makes 8,000 FE/t, and each one after it a little less: 14,000 for two, 18,000 for three and 20,000 for four, the most it counts.
- That's with the noise steady and in its sweet spot. A noise that keeps changing gets as little as half.
- It stores 2,000,000 FE and pushes up to 40,000 FE/t out of its power port, the middle of its back on the bottom layer. Only that face connects.
## Noise
It hears vibrations the way a sculk sensor does, within 8 blocks of the middle of its dish: note blocks, pistons, doors, footsteps, items landing. Its own Warden sheep moving about don't count.
- The noise level is how many vibrations it heard in the last 10 seconds, per 5 seconds. A note block struck once a second is about 5.
- The sweet spot is 5-10. Quieter, it makes less, down to nothing in silence. Louder, it loses a fifth for each level over 10.
- Wool between the noise and its dish blocks it, so wool walls keep stray noise out. A player wearing Woollen Boots makes none.
- A comparator against any block of it reads the noise level (0-15), so a circuit can turn your noise up or down.
## Keep it steady
- Too quiet for 30 seconds and its Warden sheep fall asleep and it stops. Noise back in the sweet spot wakes them, and they take 5 seconds to settle.
- Too loud for 10 seconds and the room shrieks: players nearby get Darkness, and it stops for a minute.
- A note block on a steady redstone clock, shut in with the chamber behind wool walls, is the easy way.
## Making it
- Block of Blue Steel, Sculk Wool Bale, Block of Blue Steel on top; Sculk Wool Bale, Echo Shard, Sculk Wool Bale in the middle; Blackstone, Functional Machine Block, Blackstone at the bottom.

chapters.title: Hume Field Generator
text: A 2x2 generator three blocks tall whose field can't make up its mind: every second it makes a different, random amount of power.

It fills the space east, south and above where you place it (it won't place if anything's in the way). Right-click any part of it for its window. Breaking any part takes it all down and drops the generator; a pickaxe breaks it quickly.
## Power
- Every second its field rolls a random 200 to 1,200 FE/t, 700 on average, and makes that much each tick until the next roll.

- It has no buffer. Each tick's power goes straight into whatever touches any of its twelve blocks: Energy Cables, Hume Energy Cubes, machines. Whatever they can't take that tick is lost, and nothing can pull power out of it.
- On its own it wastes everything it makes. A Hume Energy Cube against it is the easy way to catch all of it and smooth out the swings.
- Every 5 seconds its field pulses with a burst of purple sparks and a hum. Its window and Jade count down to it.
## Its window
- The gauge shows the power it makes now against its range, with its average marked. The trace shows its last rolls: purple where its power was taken, red where it was lost.
- The lamp: green when everything is taken, amber when some or all of it is wasted (its neighbours are full, or can't take that much a tick), red when nothing touching it takes power.
## Making it

- Block of Blue Steel, Tinted Glass, Block of Blue Steel on top; Hume Energy Cube, Nether Star, Hume Energy Cube in the middle; Block of Blue Steel, Functional Machine Block, Block of Blue Steel at the bottom.

chapters.title: Cables and Meter
text: ## Energy Cable
Joins generators, batteries and machines into one network moving up to 100,000 FE/t. Generators power machines first and charge cubes with the rest.
## Energy Meter

Place it between a generator or battery and what it powers: it works out which way the energy flows by itself (in at the back, out at the front). The wrench flips it. Its screens show the FE/t passing through. Right-click for the total, and read it with a comparator: the signal rises with the flow.

chapters.title: Tanks and Pipes
text: ## Fluid Tank
Holds 16 buckets of one fluid. Touching tanks join into one big tank that fills from the bottom up. Use buckets on it, or connect pipes on any side.
## Fluid Pipe
Carries fluid between anything that holds it, up to 4 buckets a tick. Machines are filled first, then tanks.
Item Pipes carry items the same way, up to 16 a tick, taking only from output slots so chests and machine inputs are never drained.

chapters.title: Energy Storage
text: A battery: 1,000,000 FE and 10,000 FE/t per cube. Touching cubes join into one bigger battery that pushes into the machines and cables around it.

chapters.title: Pipe Sides
text: Each side where a Fluid or Item Pipe meets a block can be set up on its own with the Barely Functional Wrench.
## Modes
Right-click the plug with the wrench to cycle it:
- Normal: fills the block, and only takes from pure sources such as the Automatic Shears.
- Pull (orange): empties the block, chests and tanks included.
- Push (green): only fills the block, never takes from it.
- Off: no connection. Wrench the face of the pipe's core to turn it back on.
## Filters

Sneak and right-click the plug with the wrench to open its filter: a 3x3 grid. Click a slot holding an item, or a bucket of a fluid, to filter it there; click with nothing to remove it. Only filtered things pass that side. The grid also has a mode button and a Clear button.
Shortcut: hold an item in your other hand and right-click the plug with the wrench to add it to the filter, or remove it again.

chapters.title: Wool Packer
text: The Wool Packer presses 9 of the same resource wool into one Wool Bale. Each bale takes 1,000 FE over 1 second.

Right-click it with resource wool, put wool in the left slot of its window, or feed it with a hopper or pipe. The nine pips light up as the wool for the next bale comes in. Hoppers and pipes take the bales out of any side, but never the wool.
## Separating bales

Put a whole bale in the Mechanical Separator. It takes 15 times the power of one wool, more than its 9 wool would, and as long as those 9 one at a time. In return it gives 12 wool's worth of everything: a third more resources.
An Iron Wool Bale, for example, gives 24-48 raw iron and 24 string for about 300,000 FE, where its 9 wool would give 18-36 raw iron.
Bales stack to 64, so they also carry nine times as much wool in a chest or pipe.
To get the wool back, put a bale on its own in any crafting grid: it gives its 9 wool.
## As a block
A bale can be placed like a hay bale, in the colour of its wool, and softens falls the same way. Breaking it gives the bale back.
## Config
The packer's power and speed, and what bales cost and give in the separator, are in the [wool_packer] section of the server config.

chapters.title: Wool-Lined Crate
text: A wooden crate lined with wool that holds lots of one kind of item: 2,048 of anything that stacks to 64 (32 stacks). Its front shows the item and how many. It needs no power.
- Right-click its front with an item to put it in. Right-click twice quickly to put in every one of it you're carrying.
- Left-click its front to take a stack out, or sneak-left-click to take one. Its other sides break it as usual, and so does its front once it's empty.
- Once it holds something it only takes that item, until it's empty again.
- Sneak-right-click it with an empty hand to lock it to its item: a padlock shows, and it keeps that item even when it's emptied. Again to unlock it.
- Hoppers and pipes put items in and take them out on every side. A comparator reads how full it is.
## Lining and packing
Its wool lining takes the colour of the item it holds: red for redstone, cyan for diamonds, white while it's empty. So a storeroom colour-codes itself.

Sneak-right-click it with any dyed wool to line it a colour of your own instead; it keeps that colour whatever it holds. Sneak-right-click it again with the same colour to go back to matching its item.
Sneak-right-click it with a Wool Bale to pack it in: each bale adds 32 stacks, up to 4 bales (160 stacks).
## Bursting at the seams

Past 90% full its lid bulges, wool squeezing out from under it. Once it's full, pushing more at it makes it creak, and now and then it bursts: 8 of its items fly out and its lock breaks. A pipe or hopper pushing at a full crate can burst it too.
A Crate Strap stops that for good: sneak-right-click the crate with one to strap its lid down.
## Breaking it
A crate keeps everything when it's broken: its items, lock, bales, lining and strap. Its tooltip shows what's inside. A crate with something in it can't go in another crate.
## Config
Its size, how much a bale adds, and how often it bursts are in the [crate] section of the server config.

chapters.title: Crate Controller
text: Links Wool-Lined Crates into one store, so pipes and hoppers can reach them all through one block. It needs no power.
- Crates touching it, or touching a crate already in its store, join by themselves. Build it into a wall of crates and it's done.

- For crates elsewhere, use the Barely Functional Wrench: click the controller (the wrench glows), then a crate (every crate touching it comes too), then the controller again to finish. Up to 200 blocks away.
- A store holds up to 64 crates. Crates in a store wear a little brass tag on their front, and a crate is only ever in one store.
## Pipes and hoppers
Items put into the controller go to a crate already holding them, then to an empty unlocked crate, and only then into crates whose lids are bulging. Pipes can take anything stored out of it.
If nothing fits anywhere, the fullest crate holding that item strains, and may burst, unless it's strapped.
## Keeping an eye on it

Its front shows how many crates are in its store and how full it all is: green, amber when it's nearly full or has no empty crates, red when a linked crate is missing or a full crate could burst. A comparator reads how full it all is.
Link it to a Machine Status Panel and the whole store takes one line there, and its problems set off the panel's alarm.
## Config
Its range and how many crates it holds are in the [crate_controller] section of the server config.

chapters.title: Infusing Sheep
text: Sheep are infused at a powered Infusion Altar (see its chapter): the resource in the centre, two of its blocks and a rarity item round it, and a grown sheep standing beside it.
- Its fleece takes the resource's colour, and small blocks of the resource grow out of it.
- Each infusion lasts 100 shearings by default.
- Breed infused sheep with wheat and the lamb is born infused too.
- Kill an infused sheep with its wool for a little extra.
- In creative, the Resource Wool tab has a spawn egg for every sheep, which spawns it already infused.
Right-clicking a sheep with a resource does nothing now; wheat, dyes and shears behave as usual. A server can bring hand feeding back in the config ([infusion_altar] handFeedingMaxTier).
## More resources
Data packs can add any resource, and operators can run /bfc generate to make one for every metal in the modpack. Generated sheep take 2 of the block, an ingot and a Golden Carrot.

chapters.title: Themed Sheep
text: Twelve resources turn sheep into little versions of the mob (or place) they come from:
- Hay Bale: a hay fleece (wheat).
- Snow Block: a snowy fleece, and it leaves snow wherever it walks, like a Snow Golem (snowballs).
- Nether Star: two Wither Skeleton Skulls beside its head (nether stars).
- Dragon's Breath: dragon wings (dragon's breath).
- Glow Ink Sac: a glowing fleece that lights up the ground (glow ink).
- Bone Block and Wither Rose: skull faces and bony legs (bones).
- Spider Eye: extra legs and red eyes (spider eyes).
- Echo Shard: sculk tendrils (echo shards).
- Blaze Rod: always on fire, but never hurt (blaze rods).
- Ghast Tear: twice the size, tentacles, and it screams like a ghast (ghast tears).
- Prismarine Crystals: a fin and gills; it breathes underwater and drives the Fleece Trawler (prismarine shards).
Each one has its own advancement, and collecting every wool is a challenge.

chapters.title: Infusion Altar
text: Every sheep is infused at the Infusion Altar. Put the resource in the centre slot and its catalysts in the slots round it, power the altar, and stand a grown sheep within 2 blocks of it. The sheep takes the resource when the bar fills, and the items are used up then. The altar slows the sheep down while it works, so it doesn't wander off, and lets it go once it's done.
## The recipe
Most sheep take the same pattern: the ingot (or gem, dust or item) in the centre, 2 of its blocks, and one more item for how rare the sheep is.
- Common, a Wheat: Stone, Wood, Coal, Copper, Hay, Snow, Red and Brown Mushroom.
- Uncommon, a Golden Carrot: Iron, Gold, Redstone, Lapis, Quartz, Glow Ink, Spider, Skeleton.
- Rare, a Golden Apple: Diamond, Emerald, Blaze, Ghast.
- Epic, an Eye of Ender: Netherite (with Ancient Debris), Wither Skeleton (with Nether Bricks).
For example, Iron is an Iron Ingot in the centre with 2 Blocks of Iron and a Golden Carrot. They take 20,000 FE over 2.5 seconds.
## Tier 2: legendary sheep
- Wither: Nether Star, with 4 Soul Sand, 2 Bone Blocks, 1 Wither Rose.
- Dragon: Dragon's Breath, with 4 End Stone, 4 Popped Chorus Fruit, 2 Eyes of Ender.
- Warden: Echo Shard, with 4 Sculk, 4 Amethyst Shards, 1 Sculk Catalyst.
Tier 2 takes 200,000 FE over 2.5 seconds.

The catalysts still needed show faded in the empty slots, and the Recipes tab lists every sheep's. Hoppers and pipes can feed it from any side, so it can infuse a pen without you. The spyglass button in its window, or a sneak-right-click with an empty hand, outlines the area the sheep must stand in.

When the resource and all its catalysts are in, the altar gives a one-tick redstone pulse on every side, so a dispenser or piston can bring the next sheep, or a circuit can stop the hoppers. A comparator reads its progress.
Data packs set a resource's tier, catalysts and power in its "altar" block.

chapters.title: Breeding Sheep
text: Every sheep has three stats from 1 to 10. Wild sheep are all 1s.
- Yield: more wool per shearing. Yield 10 gives about 2.35 times as much.
- Growth: sheared wool grows back on its own, without grass. At Growth 10 it takes about 11 seconds.
- Endurance: an infusion lasts more shearings. Endurance 10 makes it last 1.9 times as long.
A lamb gets the average of its parents' stats, with a 1 in 4 chance of each going up one (and a small chance of one down). Keep breeding your best sheep together to push a line up.
Sneak and right-click a sheep with an empty hand to see its stats, or look at it with Jade.
Lambs of infused sheep are born infused too, and their own Endurance counts.

chapters.title: Powered Furnace
text: Smelts anything a Furnace can, on power instead of fuel, in about a third of the time: Raw Iron takes 3.5 seconds instead of 10.
- It uses 20 FE/t while smelting, from any side.

- Blaze sheep with their fleece on, standing in the 5x5 area around it or on top, speed it up: x1.25 with one, about x1.47, x1.66 and x1.81 with two, three and four. They don't use any more power, so they save power too.
- Hoppers and pipes put items in and take results out from any side. A comparator reads the input.
- Take the results out of its window to get the smelting experience, as from a Furnace.
- Its Blaze sheep stay close: one that wanders up to 4 blocks out of the area walks back in while it has room for more.
Its spyglass button, or a sneak-right-click with an empty hand, outlines the Blaze sheep's area. JEI shows it as a station for every smelting recipe.

chapters.title: Snow Sheep Chiller
text: The Blaze Sheep Furnace's icy opposite: it freezes water into Ice with the cold of Snow sheep standing in the 5x5 area around it, on its own level or on top of it. It needs no power.
- One Snow sheep freezes a block of Ice every 5 seconds. Each extra one adds a little less: about 2.7, 1.9 and 1.5 seconds for two, three and four. It counts up to four.
- Only a grown sheep with its snowy fleece on counts; a sheared one or a lamb gives nothing until its wool grows back.
- Each Ice takes a bucket of water. Pour Water Buckets in, pipe water in, or place a Fluid Reservoir beside it. It holds 8 buckets.
- The Ice goes in its slot; a hopper or pipe can take it out of any side, and a comparator reads how full the slot is.
- Its Snow sheep stay close: one that wanders up to 4 blocks out of the area walks back in while it has room for more.

Right-click it with an empty hand to open its window: the water gauge, the cold column with a pip for each Snow sheep, the freezing arrow and how long each Ice takes. Its spyglass button, or a sneak-right-click with an empty hand, outlines the area.

chapters.title: Fleece Trawler
text: A dockside winch that fishes the pool in front of it. It needs no power: Tide sheep swimming in the pool drive it. Infuse a sheep with Prismarine Crystals at the altar (2 Prismarine and a Nautilus Shell round it) for a Tide sheep.

- Place it on the bank looking out over the water: its net faces away from you. Its pool is the water in the 7x7 in front of it, down to 4 deep; it needs at least a 3x3 two deep, and fishes faster the bigger it is.
- Each Tide sheep swimming in the pool adds speed, up to 4. A haul takes 30 seconds with one sheep in a full pool; ocean or river water and rain make it quicker.

- Hauls are fish (and now and then junk). Right-click it with resource wool for a lure: each haul then has a 30% chance of bringing up that resource instead, Raw Iron on Iron Wool, Diamonds on Diamond Wool. One wool lasts 8 resource hauls.
- Now and then its net tangles and it stops: cut it free with shears. Very rarely it drags up a confused sheep.

Right-click it with an empty hand to open its window: its lure, sheep, pool, winch and catch. Sneak-right-click it to show its pool. Take the catch from the window, or with a hopper or pipe. A comparator reads how full it is.
## Config
Its speed, pool, lures and tangles are in the [fleece_trawler] section of the server config.

chapters.title: Grass Seeder
text: Keeps a sheep pen green. Sheep eat grass down to dirt, and a sheared sheep only grows its wool back when it eats, so a bare pen is a slow pen. Place the Seeder in the middle of one.

- Every 2 seconds it tends one block of the 5x5 ground around it: dirt that's been eaten bare goes back to grass. Once it's all grass, it grows short grass on up to 40% of it, for the sheep to eat instead.
- While it has fuel, sheared sheep standing in its area graze four times as often, so their wool comes back much sooner. Sheep with their fleece on are left alone.

- Fuel: right-click it with Bone Meal (one tends 8 blocks), or feed it from a hopper or pipe. Or give it FE and water: 800 FE and 10 mB a block, from cables, pipes or a Water Bucket. It uses power and water first and saves its Bone Meal.

- With nothing to tend, it overgrows: its short grass shoots up into tall grass, which sheep can't eat and Automatic Shears can't see them in. Switch Trim on in its window (the shears button) and it cuts the tall grass back instead.
- A comparator reads how green its area is.

Right-click it with an empty hand to open its window: power and water, a map of its ground (grass, short grass, bare dirt), how green it is, its Bone Meal, and how many sheep are grazing. Its spyglass button, or a sneak-right-click with an empty hand, outlines its area. It pairs well with Automatic Shears on the same pen, and with a Static Generator, whose sheep only count with their fleece on.

chapters.title: Machine Status Panel
text: A thin screen that hangs on a wall and shows how up to 4 machines are doing, all in one place. It needs no power.
- Put panels side by side and on top of each other in a rectangle, up to 3x3, and they join into one bigger screen with 4 machines for each panel (36 on a 3x3).
- Link machines with the Barely Functional Wrench: click the panel with it (the wrench glows), then each machine within 200 blocks (again to unlink it), then the panel again to finish.

- Each machine gets two lines: its name with a lamp, then its status and one number that suits it (FE/t for a generator, progress or stored energy for the rest). Green is working, amber waiting, red a problem, grey idle. A machine that's been broken reads Missing.
- A comparator reads how many of its machines have a problem, up to 15: put a lamp or a bell on it for an alarm.

Right-click it with an empty hand for its window: name machines, move them up or down, unlink them, switch which ones' problems set off the alarm, sort the screen, change its colours, or make its comparator count working machines instead.

chapters.title: Herd Counter
text: A little screen that counts the sheep in the pen in front of it, and puts the count on a comparator. It needs no power. Place it at the edge of a pen with its screen facing in: it counts the 7x7 in front of the screen, every second.

- Right-click it with an empty hand to open its window, and pick what it counts: every sheep (SHEEP), the grown ones with their fleece on, ready to shear (READY), the sheared ones (SHORN), lambs (LAMBS), or sheep low on infusion (LOW). The screen shows the number, and a comparator reads 1 a sheep, up to 15.
- FULL reads 0 until the pen has as many sheep as its target (set with - and + in its window), then 15: handy for stopping a breeder.

- Click its filter slot with a resource wool or spawn egg to count only that resource (the label turns gold), or with an empty hand to count them all. It keeps a copy, not your item. Plain wool or a sheep's egg counts the plain sheep.
- Its window also lists the sheep of each resource in its pen, with how many are ready to shear.
- It's barely functional: a sheep dashing past its screen is now and then counted twice, making its count jump. Switch Steady on (the clock button) and it averages over 5 seconds instead.
Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to outline its area. Use it to run Automatic Shears only when enough sheep are ready, or a Grass Seeder only while sheep are shorn.

chapters.title: Wool Machines
text: ## Mechanical Separator
Put resource wool in and supply FE. Each wool gives 2 to 4 of its resource, 2 string and sometimes a bonus. Iron wool takes 20,000 FE over 2.5 seconds.
Its redstone button sets whether redstone turns it on or off. Hoppers and pipes can feed it and empty it.

It also separates Wool Bales from the Wool Packer, for more resources (see Wool Packer under Logistics). Bales use more power a tick, so it takes power in faster for them: a Wither Wool Bale needs about 3,333 FE/t.
## Automatic Shears
Shears every sheep in the 3x3 area in front of its blades, using 2,000 FE per sheep, and keeps the wool in 9 slots. Put a hopper or pipe under it to collect the wool.

chapters.title: Fluid Reservoir
text: Place it on top of an infinite water source and it fills with a bucket of water a second, which it pushes into tanks and generators beside it.

chapters.title: Upgrade Cards
text: Cards that change how a machine works. The Mechanical Separator, Wool Packer, Powered Furnace, Infusion Altar, Automatic Shears and Snow Sheep Chiller each have two upgrade slots, on the right of their window. Drag a card in, or shift-click it; one card a slot.
Craft an Upgrade Base (two at a time) from Blue Steel, Redstone and wool, then add:
- Block of Redstone, Sugar and Red Wool: Speed. Jobs take 60% of the time, for 150% of the power.
- Block of Copper and Lime Wool: Efficiency. Jobs cost 75% of the power, taking 115% of the time.
- Wool Bale and Light Blue Wool: Capacity. It holds and takes in four times the power.
- Ender Pearl and Purple Wool: Range. One more block of working area on every side (shears, altar, chiller). Its outline wobbles, and a chiller's sheep wander a bit more.
- Diamond and Yellow Wool: Yield. Each separation gives one more resource and string (separator only).
- Woollen Helmet and Black Wool: Muffler. The machine goes quiet.
A second card of the same kind does half as much. Different kinds add up: Speed and Efficiency together make jobs 69% as long for 112.5% of the power.
Cards stay with a machine when you break it or pick it up with the wrench. Hoppers and pipes never touch them.
## Config
Each card's numbers are in the [upgrades] section of the server config.

chapters.title: Work in Progress
text: Features still being built are written up here as they arrive, so you can see what's coming.

Here are the planned late-game generators, which make a lot of power but need looking after, and the Quantum Sheep. None of them can be built yet, and their numbers may change. Back up your world before trying anything here once it arrives. (The Hume Field Generator has arrived: it's in the Power tab now.)

chapters.title: Lightning Array
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; the numbers may change.
A tall copper mast, barely grounded, that catches lightning and stores it.
## Power
- Each strike gives a huge burst, around 5,000,000 FE, into Hume Energy Cubes that drain it out slowly.
## Upkeep
- It only works in thunderstorms, unless you call a strike with a Trident or a Charged Creeper head.
- Each strike oxidises the mast one stage. Scrape it with an axe or wax it; fully oxidised, it stops working.
- Sheep near a strike become Charged sheep with a crackling fleece, worth more in the Mechanical Separator.

chapters.title: Fleece Fusion
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; the numbers may change.
Fuses two different resource wools into power, such as Iron and Gold, or Coal and Netherite.
## Power
- Set by the pair: from about 5,000 FE/t for common pairs up to 50,000 FE/t for Dragon and Warden.
- The pairs and their power will be data, like Wool Burner fuels.
## Upkeep
- A steady flow of resource wool or Wool Bales, so it keeps a sheep farm busy.
- Lint builds up in its chamber. Clear it out with shears every so often; it comes out as plain wool for the Wool Burner.

chapters.title: Quantum Sheep
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; how it works may change.
A sheep that isn't sure whether it exists. Nobody is quite sure what it's infused with either, least of all the sheep.
## What it does
- Now and then it blinks out of existence for a few seconds, then pops back a few blocks away, or in the same place as if it never left.
- Each time it comes back, its wool may have changed to another resource at random.
- Shear it and every piece of wool can be a different resource, so one shearing can give Iron, Diamond and Coal Wool at once.
## The catch
- You can't choose what it gives, and the rarer resources turn up less often.
- It can't be relied on for an Automatic Shears farm: if it isn't there when the blades come round, nothing is sheared.
- Breeding two Quantum Sheep might give a Quantum lamb, a normal sheep, or both and neither.
